name: Amairgin

attributes.attribute: one of two poets of Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Two poets of Ireland share the name Amairgin. The name means new-born or song-begotten. The first Amairgin, son of Míl, was the first poet of the isle. When the Tuatha Dé Danann raised a magic storm to keep his people from landing, the words of Amairgin stilled the sea. He was the first of his folk to step on Irish moss. He sang to it his famous poem, the Song of Amairgin, in which he changes into a salmon, a sunbeam, and a blade of spear. The same power lives in his kin, the other Amairgin of Ulster. This later poet was also a warrior. He could quiet a rising fury with a glance. He was once visited by the bitter poet Aithirne, but Amairgin's words were too slippery for any satire. In the epic Táin Bó Cuailnge, Amairgin was so powerful that the dead piled up around him.
objective: Record the two Amairgins, poets of Ireland.
key_results: Show the two poets and the sea of change.
evidence: Monaghan 2003, s.v. Amairgin; Koch 2006, s.v. Amairgin
